title: Ford F-100 Engines by Year (1953–1983)
description: Every factory engine in the Ford F-100 pickup by year, 1953–1983: flathead and Y-block V8s, the 223, 240 and 300 sixes, FE 352, 360 and 390, and the 302.
intro: The F-100 was Ford's half-ton pickup from 1953 to 1983. The F-150 joined it for 1975 as a heavier-rated half-ton and replaced it after 1983. Four-wheel drive was offered from 1959 to 1976.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first F-100 used the 215 and 223 sixes and the 239 flathead V8, replaced by the overhead-valve Y-block for 1954.
The 223 six and the 272 and 292 Y-block V8s.
The 223 six and the 292 V8, then from 1965 the new 240 and 300 sixes and the FE 352 V8.
The 240 and 300 sixes, the FE 360 and 390 V8s, and the 302 from 1969. Ratings are SAE net from 1972.
Sixes and the 302, 360, 390, 351M and 400 V8s; the 460 was offered in the F-100 for 1974 only.
The last F-100s offered the 300 six, a 3.8 V6 from 1982, and the 4.2 and 5.0 V8s.
